# Error-Handling Checklist: CAR-004 Policy Controls and Adaptive Comparators

**Purpose**: Validate that the *requirements* governing escalation discipline,
signal totality, retry and cancellation bounds, platform-initiated route-change
handling, and the parent-plus-children failure fold are complete, unambiguous,
consistent, and decidable before task generation.
**Created**: 2026-07-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)
**Depth**: Standard-to-deep | **Audience**: Reviewer (PR) | **Focus**: the five
error-handling areas named in the request.

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based
on feature context and requirements. It tests the requirements, not the
implementation.

## Escalation Discipline and Route Bounds

- [x] CHK001 Is the escalation allowance stated as a hard per-objective ceiling
      rather than a rate or a default? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK002 Is "next-higher qualified route" defined by an explicitly declared
      ordered sequence rather than inferred from a model name, an alphabetical
      sort, or the bound freeze's array order? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK003 Are the consequences of a second escalation signal inside one
      objective stated — no further escalation, and termination under the frozen
      bounds? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011, §FR-014, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK004 Is wrap-around from the final ladder entry to the first refused
      explicitly rather than left to the evaluator? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-011b]
- [x] CHK005 Is a route outside the frozen candidate set required to be
      unreachable *by construction* rather than merely discouraged, and is the
      only sanctioned exclusion mechanism named? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013,
      §FR-011a.2]
- [x] CHK006 Is the ladder required to be total over the bound freeze's admitted
      tuples, so a route cannot be made unreachable by silent omission?
      [Completeness, Spec §FR-011a.2]
- [x] CHK007 Is the retry budget's behaviour across an escalation defined — does
      moving to a higher route inside one objective grant a fresh retry
      allowance, or does one allowance span every route the objective occupies?
      [Closed by §FR-014a.1] [Spec §FR-011, §FR-014]

## De-escalation, Streak Accounting, and Oscillation

- [x] CHK008 Is de-escalation constrained to objective boundaries with
      mid-objective evaluation forbidden, rather than merely discouraged?
      [Clarity, Spec §FR-012]
- [x] CHK009 Is the de-escalation threshold stated as an exact count (N = 3) and
      placed inside the control's content address rather than in the comparison
      contract? [Measurability, Spec §FR-012, Assumptions]
- [x] CHK010 Is the streak reset on a non-clean objective stated, so a broken run
      cannot be resumed rather than restarted? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012,
      Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK011 Is the streak's behaviour *after* a de-escalation fires specified —
      does one run of three clean passes license a single downward step, or does
      it license a further step at every subsequent boundary?
      [Closed by §FR-012a.4] [Spec §FR-012, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK012 Is the outcome of a de-escalation that comes due at the first ladder
      entry defined — no step, no wrap-around to the final entry, and a stated
      effect on the streak — with the same explicitness §FR-011b gives the
      ceiling? [Closed by §FR-012a.5] [Spec §FR-011b, §FR-012]
- [x] CHK013 Is it specified whether an objective in which the policy escalated
      can itself count toward the clean-pass streak? [Closed by §FR-012a.2]
      [Spec §FR-012, Assumptions]
- [x] CHK014 Is "clean pass" defined consistently across the spec and the design
      artefacts — the Assumptions entry said "no budget breach" while the data
      model requires "no budget trigger", which are different bars and decide
      whether an escalating objective counts as clean? [Conflict]
      [Closed by §FR-012a.1 and the revised Assumptions entry]
      [Spec Assumptions, data-model §1.3]
- [x] CHK015 Is the anti-oscillation guarantee stated in terms a reviewer can
      check, rather than asserted as a property of the streak reset alone?
      [Measurability, Spec §FR-012a closing paragraph, Edge Cases]

## Signal Totality and Row-Level Resolution

- [x] CHK016 Is the signal-to-response mapping required to be total over each
      declared signal domain, with neither an unmapped value nor a value
      resolving to two responses? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, §SC-003]
- [x] CHK017 Is every admitted signal required to resolve to a member the frozen
      CAR-003 contracts already publish, with no new telemetry field?
      [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, §FR-009]
- [x] CHK018 Is a rule stated for resolving a single row that carries a terminal
      state, a failure plane, and a failure code at the same time, so the row
      yields exactly one response? §FR-010's totality is per signal, not per row.
      [Closed by §FR-010b] [Spec §FR-010, data-model §1.3]
- [x] CHK019 Are the two remaining signal sources §FR-008 admits — retry count
      and raw-token/duration budget thresholds — given declared responses and a
      rank in the resolution order, rather than admitted as signals with no
      mapped response? [Closed by §FR-010b] [Spec §FR-008, §FR-010]
- [x] CHK020 Is the required relationship between the failure-plane map and the
      failure-code map stated, given the frozen contract derives the plane from
      the code so the plane map could otherwise never independently decide a
      row? [Closed by §FR-010c.1] [Spec §FR-010, data-model §1.3]
- [x] CHK021 Is the relationship between the terminal-state map and the
      failure-code map stated for candidate-plane rows, where the frozen contract
      pairs each non-completed terminal state with exactly one failure code?
      [Closed by §FR-010c.2] [Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK022 Is a membership change to a mirrored frozen enum required to fail
      the totality check closed rather than being absorbed silently?
      [Consistency, Spec §FR-010a, §SC-021]
- [x] CHK023 Is the policy-response set closed and enumerated, so "exactly one
      response" is checkable against a fixed range? [Measurability,
      Spec §FR-010, data-model §1.3]

## Retry and Cancellation Bounds

- [x] CHK024 Are retry and cancellation bounds required to be declared
      explicitly by every control rather than only by the adaptive control?
      [Coverage, Spec §FR-003, §FR-014, §FR-014a]
- [x] CHK025 Are the bounds required to be hash-relevant, so relaxing one is a
      new control version rather than an edit? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK026 Is the scope over which each bound is counted defined — per
      objective, per attempt, per agent, or over the whole parent-plus-children
      unit for the orchestration-changing control?
      [Closed by §FR-014a.1, §FR-014a.2] [Spec §FR-014, §FR-016]
- [x] CHK027 Is the outcome of a bound breach specified — which member of the
      frozen terminal-state enum and which paired failure code the breach
      records — so the §FR-016a fold and the §FR-016b acceptance floor are
      decidable on a breached run? [Closed by §FR-014a.3]
      [Spec §FR-014, §FR-016a, §FR-016b]
- [x] CHK028 Is replay proof required for the *breach* path and not only for the
      respected path, given §FR-014 asks a replay to prove the bounds "were
      respected"? [Closed by §FR-014a.4] [Spec §FR-014, §FR-028]
- [x] CHK029 Are the bound numerics required to carry their unit and comparison
      direction, so the mirror record derives them from committed bytes rather
      than transcribing them? [Traceability, Spec §FR-034.6, §FR-034a]
- [x] CHK030 Is a smoke run that reaches a declared bound mid-run required to
      stop at the bound and remain valid non-scored evidence rather than
      silently overrunning? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-030, Edge Cases]

## Platform-Initiated Route Change

- [x] CHK031 Is a platform-initiated route change required to be non-scorable
      and barred from being recorded or counted as a policy escalation?
      [Clarity, Spec §FR-015]
- [x] CHK032 Is the observable that identifies a platform-initiated route change
      bound to an already-frozen CAR-003 member, as §FR-008 requires of every
      other signal, rather than left for the implementation to choose?
      [Closed by §FR-015a] [Spec §FR-015, §FR-008]
- [x] CHK033 Is the effect of a non-scorable row on the objective's one
      escalation allowance and on the current ladder position stated, so
      platform behaviour cannot consume a policy step? [Closed by §FR-015a.1]
      [Spec §FR-015, §FR-011]
- [x] CHK034 Is the effect of a non-scorable objective on the clean-pass streak
      stated — advance, reset, or excluded — so platform behaviour can neither
      drive nor block a de-escalation? [Closed by §FR-015a.2 and §FR-012a.3]
      [Spec §FR-015, §FR-012]
- [x] CHK035 Is the disposition of an orchestration unit whose parent or any
      child was platform-rerouted defined, given the terminal-state severity
      order carries no non-scorable member? [Closed by §FR-015a.3]
      [Spec §FR-015, §FR-016a, §FR-018]

## Orchestration Aggregation Under Child Failure

- [x] CHK036 Is the aggregate terminal state defined as a worst-wins fold over
      an explicitly restated, ordered severity array rather than a projection of
      the parent's state? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016a]
- [x] CHK037 Is the severity array required to be set-equal, not order-equal, to
      the frozen terminal-state enum, and is the severity rank confined to
      aggregation so it cannot leak into the comparison? [Consistency,
      Spec §FR-016a, §FR-021b]
- [x] CHK038 Are the resources of a child that failed, timed out, or was
      cancelled required to sum into the additive dimensions rather than being
      dropped? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016, §FR-016b]
- [x] CHK039 Is aggregate acceptance floored to 0 whenever the folded terminal
      state is not `completed`, and barred from being summed, averaged,
      minimized, or maximized across children? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016b]
- [x] CHK040 Do the acceptance rules conflict when a unit both fails and never
      ran its oracle — §FR-016b requires 0, §FR-016c permits null — and is the
      precedence between them stated? [Conflict]
      [Closed by the precedence clause added to §FR-016c]
      [Spec §FR-016b, §FR-016c]
- [x] CHK041 Is the membership of the aggregation unit decidable — is
      "automatically spawned child" defined, and are a child's own children
      inside or outside the unit? [Closed by §FR-016d.1, §FR-016d.2]
      [Spec §FR-016, §FR-016a, §FR-017a]
- [x] CHK042 Is the fold's behaviour defined for a unit member that produced no
      terminal state at all, so a hung or unreported child cannot silently drop
      out of a worst-wins result? [Closed by §FR-016d.3]
      [Spec §FR-016a, §FR-016c]
- [x] CHK043 Is a zero-child run stated to be a valid row folding to the
      parent's own state rather than an error? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-016a,
      §FR-017a]
- [x] CHK044 Is a run that exceeds the declared fan-out required to be refused
      rather than aggregated, so a larger topology's cost is never charged to a
      smaller frozen identity? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-017a, §FR-016d.2]
